shared_elements: curved band motifs across the body/torso
paired symmetrical motifs flanking a central axis
belt or band across the waist
justification: Both depict a frontal, bilaterally symmetrical anthropomorphic figure with a central vertical axis, motifs flanking it, and ring/disc forms plus a girdle-like band at the waist; A adds concentric circles on the wings and B has a prominent ring on the back. But A is an elaborate winged bird-headed dancer with feathered wings, beaked mask, legs and skirt rendered in bold outline-and-infill drawing, whereas B is a low-relief carved figure of a head and body with curved incised bands and rings and no wings, beak or limbs, so the correspondences are of the generic kind any tradition could reach independently.
